d: Job Title: Senior Premium Reconciliation Specialist
Work Arrangement: 100% Remote — Work From Home

We are seeking an experienced Senior Premium Reconciliation Specialist to oversee and support the analysis, reconciliation, and monitoring of insurance premium transactions across relevant business portfolios. The role focuses on matching premium records, investigating discrepancies, reviewing financial documentation, monitoring outstanding balances, and supporting accurate premium accounting and reporting.

The successful candidate will bring strong knowledge of insurance premium administration, financial reconciliation, accounting controls, and transaction processing. Working remotely, the specialist will collaborate with finance teams, brokers, insurers, underwriting departments, and other stakeholders to maintain reliable financial records and support efficient premium settlement processes.

This position is designed as a fully remote reconciliation and financial analysis role. Physical cash or cheque handling, custody of original financial instruments, and in-person banking activities must be performed by qualified local personnel. Payment releases, premium refunds, write-offs, binding financial adjustments, and formal financial approvals must be performed or authorized by appropriately delegated finance, banking, insurance, or compliance professionals.
Perform detailed reconciliation of insurance premium records across internal systems, broker statements, insurer accounts, and financial ledgers.
Match premium transactions, receipts, commissions, adjustments, refunds, and outstanding balances against supporting documentation.
Investigate reconciliation discrepancies, duplicate entries, unmatched transactions, and unexplained financial variances.
Review premium bordereaux, broker statements, policy schedules, invoices, debit notes, credit notes, and settlement records.
Monitor premium collection status, overdue balances, unapplied receipts, and outstanding reconciliation items.
Coordinate with brokers, insurers, underwriting teams, accounts receivable, and finance departments to resolve discrepancies.
Verify the consistency of premium calculations, commission records, policy references, and transaction allocations.
Maintain accurate digital reconciliation schedules, supporting records, and audit trails.
Prepare periodic premium reconciliation reports, exception summaries, aging analysis, and management dashboards.
Support month-end, quarter-end, and year-end financial close activities through timely reconciliation and documentation.
Identify recurring transaction issues and recommend improvements to reconciliation procedures and financial controls.
Assist with internal and external audit requests by organizing supporting documentation and explaining reconciliation outcomes.
Monitor compliance with approved premium accounting procedures, internal controls, and relevant insurance requirements.
Support process automation and improvements in premium reconciliation systems and reporting workflows.
Maintain confidentiality and secure handling of financial, policyholder, broker, and commercially sensitive information.
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Insurance, or a related discipline.
Relevant professional qualifications such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA, or equivalent are an advantage.
Significant experience in insurance premium reconciliation, insurance accounting, financial operations, or accounts reconciliation.
Strong understanding of insurance premium transactions, policy administration, commissions, refunds, adjustments, and settlement processes.
Experience reconciling broker statements, insurer accounts, premium bordereaux, general ledger entries, and financial reports.
Knowledge of accounts receivable, accounts payable, aging analysis, month-end closing, and financial control procedures.
Familiarity with insurance administration platforms, ERP systems, accounting software, and advanced spreadsheet tools.
Understanding of financial governance, audit requirements, internal controls, and insurance compliance principles.
Strong numerical, analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent attention to detail and ability to identify and resolve complex reconciliation differences.
Effective written and verbal communication skills for coordinating with internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to manage multiple reconciliation schedules and deadlines independently in a remote environment.
High standards of accuracy, integrity, confidentiality, and professional accountability.
100% remote working arrangement with the flexibility to work from home.
Full-time opportunity within an insurance finance and premium operations environment.
Exposure to diverse insurance portfolios, premium accounting processes, and financial systems.
Opportunities to contribute to reconciliation accuracy, financial control improvements, and operational efficiency.
Collaboration with finance, underwriting, broker management, and insurance operations professionals.
Opportunities for continued professional development and career advancement.

Interested candidates should submit an updated CV highlighting their premium reconciliation experience, accounting qualifications, insurance operations knowledge, and expertise in financial reporting and transaction analysis.
Application Email Subject: Application – Senior Premium Reconciliation Specialist (UAE Remote)
Candidates should confirm applicable employment arrangements, residency requirements, and work authorization before accepting an offer.

Important Scope Note: This is a fully remote specialist role focused on reconciliation analysis, transaction matching, financial documentation review, discrepancy investigation, reporting, and virtual coordination. Physical cash or cheque handling, custody of original financial instruments, and in-person banking activities must be carried out by qualified local personnel. Payment releases, premium refunds, write-offs, settlement agreements, binding financial adjustments, general ledger approvals, regulated financial decisions, formal financial statement certifications, regulatory filings, and statutory sign-offs must be performed or approved by appropriately authorized finance, banking, insurance, or compliance professionals.
